avoid planters, gardens and grassed areas immediately adjacent to buildings on high level footings and extend pavements around the perimeter to reduce differential movement Excavate, clean, inspect and pour footings with minimum delay, or protect the base with at least 75 mm of blinding concrete, and prevent ponding in footing excavations Adopt a design subgrade CBR of 4% (or 40 MPa short term modulus) for internal roads and confirm traffic loading before finalising pavement design; inspect the subgrade after preliminary boxing to identify stabilisation requirements Blend, treat, or lime/gypsum stabilise soils with ESP over 15% before reuse, and provide surface drainage control, vegetative cover and erosion protection (turfing, geofabric in concentrated flow paths) during construction Maintain surface drainage, minimise uncontrolled fill and protect exposed soils with turf or erosion matting to manage shallow slumping and rutting in the soft near surface zones Manage ongoing erosion and shallow bank instability along Macquarie Rivulet through surface drainage, vegetation maintenance and setback of engineered fill and structures from the top of bank Install temporary surface drainage (interceptor drains, sump pumping) where seepage or ponding occurs and incorporate permanent subsoil drainage in detailed design; provide subsoil drains around pavement perimeters with inverts at least 200 mm below subgrade Install a network of roughly 6 to 8 standpipe piezometers and monitor groundwater seasonally to confirm design levels for pavements, building platforms and retaining wall drainage Carry out a detailed geotechnical investigation at final design levels before detailed design of retaining walls and road pavements Inspect any excavation deeper than 1.5 m, review structural drawings, and re engage the geotechnical engineer if conditions or the design change significantly Stated limitations Scope of services may have been limited or amended by time, budget, access and site constraints The report is for the exclusive use of Environmental Group Australia Pty Ltd for the specific development and purpose described and may not contain sufficient information for other purposes, developments or sites Information is considered accurate only at the date of issue with regard to conditions at that time Conclusions rely on interpolation between test pits and conditions can vary between test locations Depths and layer thicknesses in Table 2 apply at the investigation locations and may not represent the whole site CG relied on information provided by the client and their agents and has not verified its accuracy or completeness The report should not be used as part of a project specification without CG's review and agreement, being advice and opinion rather than construction instructions The report must be kept whole and read with the attached Information Sheets and explanatory notes Groundwater levels may not have stabilised over the short observation period and fluctuate with rainfall, temperature and other factors; no longer term monitoring was carried out The AS 2870 site classification is preliminary and must be reassessed after earthworks and before building pad construction Pavement designs are preliminary; traffic loadings require confirmation by the client and final material and compaction specifications must be set by the pavement designer Only ESP testing was undertaken to assess dispersive potential (no Emerson or dispersion testing) Suitability of the site remains contingent on implementing the recommended earthworks, drainage, foundation and groundwater control measures, and CG accepts no responsibility for changed site conditions, design modifications or construction practices outside the scope of the assessment without further review Site specific advice from an experienced geotechnical engineer is required for permanent slope batters Reviewer flags Report body extracted cleanly and the parameter tables are legible; the test pit logs are not. Points to verify against the source PDF: (1) Fieldwork date conflict the body states 6 and 7 August 2025, but all 26 test pit log headers read 'DATE STARTED 6/7/25 COMPLETED 6/7/25', which reads as 6 July 2025 in Australian format. The ISO date given here is the report issue date (6 October 2025), which is unambiguous. (2) Depth to rock is inconsistent: Table 2 lists bedrock in TP02, TP04, TP17, TP20 and TP25 and Section 10.1 puts it at about 1.7 m to 2.1 m, yet the TP17 and TP25 logs terminate at 1.0 m and the TP04 log shows sandstone from 1.0 m (RL 23.5) with termination at 1.7 m. Rockhead depths should be re read from the original logs. (3) Section 8.1 gives a plasticity index range of 5.5% to 62%, but the minimum PI in Table 3 is 11% 5.5% is the minimum linear shrinkage, so the PI lower bound appears to be a transcription slip. (4) Table 1 lists 7 Atterberg/linear shrinkage tests while Table 3 reports only 6 sets of LL/PI/LS results. (5) Section 8.6 and Section 9.1 refer to 35 EC/pH samples, but the extracted Table 8 contains only 16 unique rows plus duplicate TP01 (0.3 0.5) and TP02 (0.8 1.0) rows repeated at the foot of the table the full table may not have carried through the extraction. (6) The test pit logs are column collapsed in the extracted text: DCP entries appear as isolated 'DCP = 1' / 'DCP = 2' markers with loose blow count digits floating beside the strata descriptions, so per depth DCP profiles and the water level symbols cannot be reconstructed reliably. Only the summary statement of 1 to 2 blows per 100 mm in the upper 0.8 m and the 19 'NONE ENCOUNTERED' water annotations can be relied on. (7) Section 7.2 cites the Wollongong 1:250,000 Sheet SI 56 9 Second Edition 1966, while reference item 8 cites the Wollongong Port Hacking 1:100,000 Sheet 9029 9129 (Edition 1) 1985. (8) Section 10.2 refers to 'Australian Geogrids LR8' where the appendix list and AGS publication name is Australian Geoguide LR8. (9) Section 8.3 concludes the tested soils are 'silty clays of low plasticity' and suitable for engineered fill, which sits awkwardly against the LL up to 84%, PI up to 62% and the H1 H2 reactivity assessment elsewhere in the report. (10) No allowable bearing pressure is given for footings founded directly on the weathered sandstone or conglomerate, and no pile capacities are provided despite deep foundations being in the stated scope. (11) Table 1 lists 36 FMC tests; Section 8.1 accounts for 34 soil plus 2 sandstone samples, but Table 3 lists 39 rows the count should be checked. (12) A design CBR of 4% is adopted although all four measured CBR values were 8% to 20%; this is conservative but the report does not state the basis for the reduction. notes.title: CG25-1033-A - Leachate plant upgrade, Erskine Park
notes.body:
# CG25-1033-A - Leachate plant upgrade, Erskine Park

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG25-1033-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG25-1033-A Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2025-10-27 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | H & H Consulting Engineers (H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd), Suite 2.01, 828 Pacific Highway, Gordon NSW 2072 |
| Site | 85 Quarry Road, Erskine Park NSW (described elsewhere in the report as 85-87 Quarry Road; part of the Cleanaway Erskine Park Landfill / Waste & Resource Management Facility, Penrith City Council LGA) |
| Project | Upgrade of the existing leachate treatment plant: a new circular tank approximately 11.5 m diameter holding up to 1.1 ML, sited west of the existing plant, plus a new access road on the eastern side |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation (foundation and preliminary pavement advice, soil aggressivity assessment, with a subcontracted waste classification appended) |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Core Geotech was engaged under proposal QU25-0381 Rev 0 (1 August 2025) to carry
out a desktop review, drill and log a borehole programme, schedule laboratory
testing, and build a ground model for the wastewater treatment plant upgrade.
Deliverables asked for were subsurface descriptions, suitable foundation options
with design parameters, pavement design parameters, and an assessment of soil
aggressivity. A waste classification of excavated material was commissioned
separately from Development Risk Management Pty Ltd.

## Fieldwork

- Site walkover survey to assess landform and surface conditions
- Underground services search by a specialist contractor prior to drilling
- 5 boreholes (BH01 to BH05) drilled with a track-mounted rig using 120 mm solid flight auger; termination depths 3.0 m to 8.5 m
- BH01 to BH04 each terminated at 3.0 m; BH05 terminated at 8.5 m
- Fieldwork on 25 September 2025 (BH01-BH04, drilled by Geotrace Australia Pty Ltd) and 3 October 2025 (BH05, drilled by Pace Drilling Services Pty Ltd)
- SPTs at regular intervals in all boreholes (BH01 N=8/32/29; BH02 N=9 and 6,12,14/80 mm double bounce; BH03 N=8/30; BH04 N=14/41; BH05 N=11/27/20/40 and 5,14/60 mm double bounce at 7.0 m)
- Disturbed sampling with Chain of Custody to NATA-accredited laboratories; boreholes backfilled with quick-set concrete
- Laboratory schedule: 1 CBR (AS 1289.6.1.1), 2 aggressivity soil suites (APHA), 11 field moisture contents (AS 1289.2.1.1), by Eurofins Environment Testing Australia and Benchmark Geotechnical
- Logging and descriptions in general accordance with AS 1726 (2017)

## Subsurface profile as logged

- FILL - sandy GRAVEL / silty sandy CLAY / silty CLAY, medium to high plasticity, fine to medium grained sand and gravel, grey and brown, moisture condition at or below plastic limit; base of layer 0.3 m to 4.0 m. Thin (about 0.3-0.6 m) across BH01-BH04 on the eastern side; about 4 m thick at BH05 in the proposed tank footprint. Treated as uncontrolled fill (no compaction records).
- RESIDUAL CLAY - medium to high plasticity, brown, pale grey, orange and yellow, trace ironstone gravel and shale fragments, moisture condition at or below plastic limit; base of layer stated as >3.0 m to 7.2 m. Logged stiff near surface grading very stiff to hard with depth.
- BEDROCK - SILTSTONE, extremely weathered, fine grained, pale grey to brown, trace high plasticity fines, very low to low strength; encountered in BH05 only, from about 7.0 m to the 8.5 m hole termination (Table 2 gives base of layer as >8.5 m).

## Rock

Extremely weathered siltstone reached only in BH05, at approximately 7.0 m
depth, and proved to the 8.5 m termination. Described as fine grained, pale grey
to brown, very low to low strength, with trace high plasticity clay; SPT in the
unit recorded 5, 14 for 60 mm with double bounce. BH01-BH04 were terminated at
3.0 m in residual clay without reaching rock. No RLs are given (surface RL and
datum fields on all logs are blank). Table 6 design parameters label the same
unit 'Bringelly Shale, Class V'.

## Groundwater

Not encountered. All five borehole logs (25 September and 3 October 2025) are
annotated 'GROUNDWATER NOT ENCOUNTERED'. The report cautions that standing water
and seepage can fluctuate with rainfall, temperature and other factors, and
states no long-term groundwater monitoring was carried out.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Allowable end bearing pressure - Bringelly Shale, Class V (socketed bored pier) | 700 | kPa |
| Ultimate shaft adhesion - Bringelly Shale, Class V | 50 | kPa |
| Design Young's modulus - Bringelly Shale, Class V | 50 | MPa |
| Ultimate shaft adhesion - residual clay | 30 | kPa |
| Design Young's modulus - residual clay | 15 | MPa |
| Allowable bearing pressure - residual clay | not provided (shown as '-' in Table 6) |  |
| Minimum rock socket length into low to very low strength siltstone (piles in BH05 area) | 2 | m |
| Expected total settlement under serviceability load | <1% of footing width or pile diameter |  |
| Expected differential settlement between adjacent columns | less than half of the total settlement |  |
| Soaked CBR - BH01, 0.7-0.9 m, silty clay/residual | 1.5 | % |
| Swell on CBR sample | 5.0 | % |
| Maximum dry density (MDD) - CBR sample | 1.79 | t/m3 |
| Optimum moisture content (OMC) - CBR sample | 17 | % |
| Field moisture content at CBR sample | 15.9 | % |
| Field moisture content range across tested samples | 7.9 to 18.5 | % |
| Subgrade compaction target after boxing and proof rolling | >=100% Standard compaction at SOMC +/- 2% |  |
| Confirmatory soaked CBR tests required on prepared formation | at least 2 | tests |
| Exposure classification - concrete piles, AS 2159-2009 Table 6.4.2(C) | mild |  |
| Exposure classification - steel piles, AS 2159-2009 Table 6.5.2(C) | mild |  |
| Soil permeability type for aggressivity assessment | Type B (low permeability) |  |
| pH - BH01 0.5-0.95 m clay/residual | 7.4 | pH |
| pH - BH05 7.0-7.45 m siltstone/bedrock | 8.7 | pH |
| Conductivity - BH01 / BH05 | 13 / 92 | uS/cm |
| Resistivity - BH01 / BH05 | 800 / 110 | Ohm.m |
| Chloride - BH01 / BH05 | <10 / 92 | ppm |
| Sulphate - BH01 / BH05 | <10 / <10 | ppm |
| AS 2870-2011 site classification | not assigned - report states the tank falls outside the scope of AS 2870 |  |
| Waste classification (DRM P25.1033-R01) - fill near BH02/BH03 to about 0.3 m within the mapped polygon | Restricted Solid Waste (non-putrescible) |  |
| Waste classification - residual soils near BH02/BH03 to about 0.6 m | General Solid Waste (non-putrescible) |  |
| Waste classification - fill outside the RSW polygon | General Solid Waste (non-putrescible) |  |
| Waste classification - residual clays beneath the fill | VENM, subject to appropriate confirmatory testing |  |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Treat all fill on site as uncontrolled under AS 3798-2007 because no placement or compaction records exist.
- Do not rely on shallow footings for the tank - roughly 4 m of uncontrolled fill at BH05 plus adjacent sensitive assets (leachate plant, retaining walls) make settlement performance unacceptable.
- Use piles to carry the tank loads down to competent ground; bored piles, CFA and screw piles are all listed as viable options.
- Socket piles in the BH05 area at least 2 m into the low to very low strength siltstone, going deeper where ultimate or serviceability checks demand it.
- Design piles to AS 2159, using shaft friction, end bearing and modulus values for Sydney Basin siltstone from Pells et al. (2019) as tabulated, and allow for potential downdrag through the fill.
- Check serviceability for both individual and group piles, including rotations, allowing for group interaction and stress bulb overlap.
- Case through the uncontrolled fill, keep the socket stable, roughen socket walls, and tremie concrete or grout under fluid to avoid segregation; socket base and walls must be clean and sound before pouring.
- Have a geotechnical consultant inspect and approve bored pile bearing and socket depths before concreting; allow for temporary steel casing if water is met in the clay during drilling.
- For the access road, base preliminary design on the prepared formation rather than in-situ conditions; proof roll after boxing, rework to SOMC +/- 2%, compact to at least 100% Standard, maintain drainage and carry out density and moisture QA.
- Obtain at least two confirmatory soaked CBR tests on the prepared formation at the design surcharge to verify the characteristic design value.
- Where weak or highly plastic material is exposed, undercut and replace with select material or stabilise in situ (granular capping, lime or lime-cement), with extent confirmed by the geotechnical consultant after boxing.
- Adopt concrete and steel appropriate to a 'mild' AS 2159-2009 exposure classification for both concrete and steel piles.
- Refer tank foundation design to AS 3798, AS 2159, AS 3600 and the relevant tank code rather than AS 2870.
- Have CG review the architectural, civil and structural drawings to confirm the report's recommendations have been carried into the design.
- Clear all footings of debris and softened material, have them designed by a structural engineer, and have them inspected and approved before concrete is poured.
- Seek further advice if ground conditions differ materially from those described, or if the project scope changes significantly.
- Have an experienced person inspect the stability of any excavation deeper than 1.0 m.
- (From the DRM waste report) Dispose of excess soil to a licensed landfill per the assigned classifications, keep VENM residual clay separate from fill so the classification is not voided, stop work and consult the environmental consultant if contamination indicators appear, and retain disposal records for the NSW EPA.

## Stated limitations

- Scope of services was set by the proposal and may have been constrained by time, budget, access and site constraints.
- Report is for the exclusive use of H & H Consulting Engineers and only for the development and purpose described; it may not hold enough information for any other purpose or site.
- Findings are accurate at the date of issue for the conditions then present; subsurface conditions can change over time.
- Conclusions rest on interpolation between borehole locations, and conditions between test points can vary in ways no investigation can fully reveal.
- Depths and layer thicknesses in the summary table apply at the investigation points and may not represent the whole site.
- CG relied on information supplied by the client and their agents and did not verify its accuracy or completeness.
- Groundwater levels on logs are point-in-time records; actual levels may differ over longer periods and can shift seasonally or with construction.
- No long-term groundwater monitoring was undertaken.
- Soil and rock descriptions are based on visual and tactile assessment to AS 1726-2017, except where field or laboratory testing was done.
- The report is advice and opinion, not construction instructions, and should not be used in a specification without CG's review and agreement.
- The report must be kept whole and read with the attached information sheets and explanatory notes; individual pages or sections should not be separated.
- CG accepts no responsibility for third-party interpretations of the report or test data that the report does not itself support.
- Architectural and civil drawings were not available at the time of reporting; the development description came from discussions with the client.
- AS 2870-2011 does not cover the proposed tank, so no site classification applies to it.

## Reviewer flags

Text extraction was clean for the narrative and mostly readable for the tables,
but several internal inconsistencies in the source document are worth flagging.
(1) Section 1 describes the work as being for a 'proposed residential
development', which contradicts the industrial wastewater treatment plant
project - likely template carry-over. (2) Section 8.1 states nine (9) FMC
samples were tested, but Table 3 lists 11 results and Table 1 schedules 11. (3)
Address conflict: the CG report gives 85 Quarry Road (and 85-87 Quarry Road)
Erskine Park, while the appended DRM waste classification report (Ref. DRM
P25.1033-R01, 27 October 2025, though internally dated 20 October 2025 on one
figure) gives 4 Quarry Road, Erskine Park, Lot 4 DP1094504 - reviewer should
confirm which is correct. (4) Unit naming conflict: Table 2 and the BH05 log
call the bedrock SILTSTONE, but the Table 6 design parameter row is labelled
'Bringelly Shale, Class V'; presumably the same material, but the report never
states this explicitly. (5) Section 10.2 is headed 'Preliminary AS2870-2011 Site
Classification' yet gives no site class at all - it only says the tank is
outside AS 2870's scope. No classification (M, H1 etc.) is stated anywhere for
the site. (6) All borehole logs have blank R.L. SURFACE and DATUM fields, so no
reduced levels are available anywhere in the report; all depths are metres below
ground. (7) Table 2 depth ranges are awkwardly written ('>3.0 - 7.2' for
residual, '>8.5' for bedrock) and do not obviously reconcile with the BH05 log,
which shows siltstone from about 7.0 m to termination at 8.5 m; the bedrock base
was never proved. (8) Table 5 (aggressivity) had vertically rotated column
headers that interleaved in extraction; I mapped values by order and cross-
checked that conductivity and resistivity are reciprocal (13 uS/cm vs 800 Ohm.m;
92 uS/cm vs 110 Ohm.m), which confirms the mapping - but note BH05 chloride (92
ppm) and BH05 conductivity (92 uS/cm) share the same figure, which could
conceivably be a transcription error in the original and is worth checking
against the Eurofins certificate. (9) Table 6 gives no allowable bearing
pressure for residual clay (shown as '-'). (10) The DRM report footnote records
that 8 boreholes were originally proposed but 3 could not be drilled because of
access restrictions - the CG report does not mention this reduction in coverage.
(11) Minor typos in the source: 'trace irstone gravel' (ironstone), 'shale
fragmnets', 'extrremely weathered', 'non-putrecible'. (12) Only one CBR test
supports the pavement advice, and the report itself calls the value preliminary.
(13) The exact tank footprint location relative to BH05 is not dimensioned in
the extracted text; the site plan (Drawing CG25/1033-1) is an image and could
not be read.

The report itself is not reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source. : : Report CG25 1033 A Rev 0 Issued 2025 10 27 Author Core Geotech Pty Ltd Client H & H Consulting Engineers (H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd), Suite 2.01, 828 Pacific Highway, Gordon NSW 2072 Site 85 Quarry Road, Erskine Park NSW (described elsewhere in the report as 85 87 Quarry Road; part of the Cleanaway Erskine Park Landfill / Waste & Resource Management Facility, Penrith City Council LGA) Project Upgrade of the existing leachate treatment plant: a new circular tank approximately 11.5 m diameter holding up to 1.1 ML, sited west of the existing plant, plus a new access road on the eastern side Document type geotechnical investigation (foundation and preliminary pavement advice, soil aggressivity assessment, with a subcontracted waste classification appended) Extraction confidence high Scope Core Geotech was engaged under proposal QU25 0381 Rev 0 (1 August 2025) to carry out a desktop review, drill and log a borehole programme, schedule laboratory testing, and build a ground model for the wastewater treatment plant upgrade. Deliverables asked for were subsurface descriptions, suitable foundation options with design parameters, pavement design parameters, and an assessment of soil aggressivity. A waste classification of excavated material was commissioned separately from Development Risk Management Pty Ltd. Fieldwork Site walkover survey to assess landform and surface conditions Underground services search by a specialist contractor prior to drilling 5 boreholes (BH01 to BH05) drilled with a track mounted rig using 120 mm solid flight auger; termination depths 3.0 m to 8.5 m BH01 to BH04 each terminated at 3.0 m; BH05 terminated at 8.5 m Fieldwork on 25 September 2025 (BH01 BH04, drilled by Geotrace Australia Pty Ltd) and 3 October 2025 (BH05, drilled by Pace Drilling Services Pty Ltd) SPTs at regular intervals in all boreholes (BH01 N=8/32/29; BH02 N=9 and 6,12,14/80 mm double bounce; BH03 N=8/30; BH04 N=14/41; BH05 N=11/27/20/40 and 5,14/60 mm double bounce at 7.0 m) Disturbed sampling with Chain of Custody to NATA accredited laboratories; boreholes backfilled with quick set concrete Laboratory schedule: 1 CBR (AS 1289.6.1.1), 2 aggressivity soil suites (APHA), 11 field moisture contents (AS 1289.2.1.1), by Eurofins Environment Testing Australia and Benchmark Geotechnical Logging and descriptions in general accordance with AS 1726 (2017) Subsurface profile as logged FILL sandy GRAVEL / silty sandy CLAY / silty CLAY, medium to high plasticity, fine to medium grained sand and gravel, grey and brown, moisture condition at or below plastic limit; base of layer 0.3 m to 4.0 m. Thin (about 0.3 0.6 m) across BH01 BH04 on the eastern side; about 4 m thick at BH05 in the proposed tank footprint. Treated as uncontrolled fill (no compaction records). Logged stiff near surface grading very stiff to hard with depth. Young's modulus Bringelly Shale, Class V 50 MPa Ultimate shaft adhesion residual clay 30 kPa Design Young's modulus residual clay 15 MPa Allowable bearing pressure residual clay not provided (shown as ' ' in Table 6) Minimum rock socket length into low to very low strength siltstone (piles in BH05 area) 2 m Expected total settlement under serviceability load <1% of footing width or pile diameter compaction target after boxing and proof rolling =100% Standard compaction at SOMC +/ 2% Confirmatory soaked CBR tests required on prepared formation at least 2 tests Exposure classification concrete piles, AS 2159 2009 Table 6.4.2(C) mild Exposure classification steel piles, AS 2159 2009 Table 6.5.2(C) mild Soil permeability type for aggressivity assessment Type B (low permeability) pH BH01 0.5 0.95 m clay/residual 7.4 pH pH BH05 7.0 7.45 m siltstone/bedrock 8.7 pH Conductivity BH01 / BH05 13 / 92 uS/cm Resistivity BH01 / BH05 800 / 110 Ohm.m Chloride BH01 / BH05 <10 / 92 ppm Sulphate BH01 / within the mapped polygon Restricted Solid Waste (non putrescible) Waste classification residual soils near BH02/BH03 to about 0.6 m General Solid Waste (non putrescible) Waste classification fill outside the RSW polygon General Solid Waste (non putrescible) Waste classification residual clays beneath the fill VENM, subject to appropriate confirmatory testing These are the report's numbers, not this vault's. They apply to the site, loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own limitations. Re derive or re check before using them anywhere else. Recommendations Treat all fill on site as uncontrolled under AS 3798 2007 because no placement or compaction records exist. Do not rely on shallow footings for the tank roughly 4 m of uncontrolled fill at BH05 plus adjacent sensitive assets (leachate plant, retaining walls) make settlement performance unacceptable. Use piles to carry the tank loads down to competent ground; bored piles, CFA and screw piles are all listed as viable options. Socket piles in the BH05 area at least 2 m into the low to very low strength siltstone, going deeper where ultimate or serviceability checks demand it. Design piles to AS 2159, using shaft friction, end bearing and modulus values for Sydney Basin siltstone from Pells et al. (2019) as tabulated, and allow for potential downdrag through the fill. Check serviceability for both individual and group piles, including rotations, allowing for group interaction and stress bulb overlap. Have an experienced person inspect the stability of any excavation deeper than 1.0 m. notes.body:
# CG25-1096-A - Subdivision, Riverstone

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG25-1096-A Rev 3.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG25-1096-A Rev 3 |
| Issued | 2025-09-18 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | Development Risk Management Pty Ltd, Suite 14, 265-271 Pennant Hills Road, Thornleigh NSW 2120 (development applicant: Austral South Nominee Pty Ltd) |
| Site | 32 Cranbourne Street, Riverstone NSW - Lot 4 Sec H DP 712, plus adjoining road reserves in Cranbourne Street, Grandeur Parade and Kensington Park Road (Blacktown City Council LGA) |
| Project | Proposed Residential Subdivision - 39 Torrens title lots and 10 community title lots |
| Document type | geotechnical and salinity investigation with preliminary AS2870 site classification |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Test-pit investigation and laboratory programme supporting a DA for residential
subdivision. CG assessed the soil and rock profile, salinity and sodicity,
preliminary AS2870 site classification, earthworks and farm-dam removal,
retaining wall and footing parameters, and pavement subgrade strength.

## Fieldwork

- Fieldwork carried out 29 August 2025 under CG direction, logged to AS1726 (2017)
- Walkover survey of the lot
- Ten test pits TP01 to TP10 excavated to termination/refusal depths of 1.5m to 2.5m using a 5 tonne tracked excavator with a 450mm bucket
- Dynamic Cone Penetrometer tests adjacent to the test pits
- Disturbed samples collected and sent to NATA accredited laboratories under Chain of Custody

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Topsoil: Silty CLAY, medium to high plasticity, dark grey, trace fine grained sand, gravel and organics, moisture >= plastic limit; base 0.2 - 0.5m
- Residual: CLAY / Silty CLAY, medium to high plasticity, red, orange, pale grey, some shale fragments, moisture >= plastic limit; base 1.0 - >1.5m
- Bedrock: SHALE, extremely weathered, fine to medium grained, dark grey, very low to low strength, Class V (TP01 and TP03 to TP10 only); base >1.5 - >2.5m

## Rock

Extremely weathered Bringelly Shale, very low to low strength, Class V,
encountered in nine of ten test pits (TP01, TP03 to TP10) at 1.0m to 1.8m below
existing surface. Higher strength shale may lie below test pit refusal level.
Foundation parameters given for Class V Bringelly Shale only.

## Groundwater

No free groundwater encountered during the investigation. Standing groundwater
and seepage may fluctuate with rainfall and temperature. No long-term
groundwater monitoring undertaken.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Field Moisture Content range (9 samples) | 18.6 to 27.5 | % |
| Liquid Limit, TP04 0.5-0.7m and TP09 0.8-1.0m | 73 and 64 | % |
| Plasticity Index, TP04 and TP09 | 50 and 42 | % |
| Linear Shrinkage, TP04 and TP09 | 17 and 16 | % |
| CBR, TP06 1.0-1.2m Clay/Residual | 3.5 | % |
| Design CBR adopted for Grandeur Parade pavement | 3 | % |
| CBR sample OMC / MDD / swell | 17.5% OMC, 1.77 t/m3 MDD, 1.5% swell | - |
| ECe range across 35 samples | 0.11 to 5.69 | dS/m |
| Salinity distribution | 30 samples (86%) <2 dS/m; 2 samples (6%) 2-3.99 dS/m; 3 samples (8%) 4-7.99 dS/m | - |
| ESP range (4 samples) | 7.0 to 28.7 | % |
| Cation Exchange Capacity range (4 samples) | 5.4 to 11.0 | meq/100g |
| AS2870-2011 site classification | Class P (due to abnormal moisture from trees and existing structures); Class H1/H2 in the absence of abnormal moisture | - |
| Characteristic surface movement ys of natural soil | 40 to 75 | mm |
| Suction change / suction depth used | 1.2 pF change, 1.5m suction depth | - |
| Allowable bearing pressure, controlled fill or very stiff natural clay | 100 | kPa |
| Minimum footing embedment for the 100 kPa ABP | 0.8 | m below surrounding ground level |
| Allowable bearing pressure, Bringelly Shale Class V | 700 | kPa |
| Ultimate shaft adhesion, Bringelly Shale Class V | 50 | kPa |
| Design Young's modulus, Bringelly Shale Class V | 50 | MPa |
| Minimum rock socket for piers | 0.3 | m |
| Engineered fill compaction | 95% to 99% SMDD, moisture within 2% of SOMC, max 300mm loose layers, min 12 tonne padfoot roller, max particle size 75mm | - |
| Trench backfill | max 150mm loose layers, max particle size 50mm | - |
| Retained material bulk unit weight for permanent walls | 18 | kN/m3 |
| Earth pressure parameters, Residual Clay/Silty Clay | 18 kN/m3, phi' 26 deg, E' 20 MPa, K0 0.50, Ka 0.39, Kp 2.56 | - |
| Earth pressure parameters, Shale rock Class V | 20 kN/m3, phi' 30 deg, E' 50 MPa, K0 0.50, Ka 0.33, Kp 3.00 | - |
| Temporary batter slopes (H:V), cuts to 3m | 1.5:1 controlled fill and very stiff residual silty/clay; 1.25:1 Class V shale | - |
| Anticipated earthworks | generally up to 1m cut and 1.5m fill; about 2 to 3m fill over the two farm dams | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Adopt Class P now because of abnormal moisture conditions; reassess differential movement after earthworks and before building pad construction, with slabs designed by engineering principles
- Decommission and desilt the two farm dams: divert upstream water permanently, dewater, desilt and dry the material, remove soft/compressible zones, test roll under geotechnical supervision, then backfill as engineered fill
- Re-use excavated residual soil and shale as engineered fill if clean, organic-free and under 75mm particle size, subject to environmental approval
- Compact engineered fill in 300mm loose layers to 95-99% SMDD within 2% of SOMC; extend each layer 1m beyond design geometry for edge compaction and trim back afterwards
- Backfill service trenches in 150mm loose layers with 50mm maximum particle size, compacted with trench roller, padfoot attachment or rammer
- Density test at one per layer per 2500 m2 or one per 500 m3 or 3 tests per lot, whichever gives most tests; trench backfill at one test per two layers per 40 linear metres; Level 1 supervision for fill supporting buildings, Level 2 for pavements
- Consider vibration controls where fill placement is within about 15m of nearby buildings, including a static rolling exclusion zone
- Cover exposed clay and shale faces with waterproof membrane; keep surcharge at least 2.5H from batter crests; retain excavations deeper than 1.5m
- Use 100 kPa allowable bearing pressure only for footings at least 0.8m deep in controlled fill or very stiff natural clay, not underlain by uncontrolled fill; avoid planters and gardens against the building
- Where piles are used, bored piers are the preferred option, socketed at least 0.3m into Class V Bringelly Shale with clean, rough (R2) sockets
- Design pavements on Grandeur Parade for CBR 3%; Road No. 1 is entirely in fill so its design CBR cannot be confirmed until fill is placed and tested; take further CBR samples after boxing out
- If services are excavated deeper than about 1.3m near TP10, design buried concrete/steel for AS 3600 Class A2 or higher exposure and undertake confirmatory salinity testing
- Undertake additional subsurface investigation and proof rolling where existing rural-residential dwellings may overlie undocumented fill

## Stated limitations

- Prepared for the exclusive use of Development Risk Management Pty Ltd for the described development
- Conclusions based on interpolation between test pits; conditions can vary between test locations
- Not to be used as part of a project specification without CG review and agreement
- Must be read in its entirety with the attached Information Sheets
- Assumes no buildings or structures near the central high-voltage transmission corridor
- Site classification recommendations assume AS2870-2011 performance expectations are acceptable and CSIRO BTF-18 maintenance is followed
- Design parameters may need reassessment because better shale may occur below test pit refusal depth

## Reviewer flags

The salinity (Table 6), aggressivity (Table 5) and ESP/CEC (Table 7) tables are
column-scrambled in the extraction; values were recovered by matching the header
order and are reported here in that interpretation - worth a visual check
against the PDF. Minor internal inconsistencies: Table 1 lists FMC quantity as 8
while Section 8.1 and Table 3 report nine samples; Section 10.8 cites 'Table 6'
for aggressivity results that appear in Table 5; the sentence in Section 10.6.1
about shrink-swell movements is left incomplete in the source. Revision history:
Rev 0 12.09.2025, Rev 1 16.09.2025, Rev 2 and Rev 3 both 18.09.2025. Author
Gopinath Naga, reviewer Raj Singh. Moderately saline soils are confined to TP10
at about 1.3m to 2.5m depth.

## Standards cited

AS1726-2017 Geotechnical Site Investigation, AS2870-2011 Residential slabs and footings, AS3798-2007 Guidelines on earthworks for commercial and residential developments, AS4678-2002 Earth-retaining structures, AS1289.6.1.1 (CBR), AS1289 3.1.2/3.2.1/3.3.1/3.4.1 (Atterberg and linear shrinkage), AS1289 2.1.1 (FMC), APHA (aggressivity, ESP/CEC, EC/pH), AS 3600 (exposure classification referenced for buried concrete), HB 160-2006 Soils testing (reconfirmed 2016), WSROC Salinity Code of Practice (salinity rating scale), Pells, Mostyn, Bertuzzi and Wong, Classification of Sandstones and Shales in the Sydney Region: A forty year review, Vol 54 No 2, June 2019, Walker and Pells (1998) socket roughness R2, CSIRO BTF-18 (Foundation Maintenance Homeowner's Guide), Penrith 1:100,000 Geological Series Sheet 9030 (Edition 1) 1991, NSW Environment & Heritage eSPADE

notes.body:
# CG25-1240-C - Mascot hotel basement (draft)

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG25-1240-C_DRAFT.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG25-1240-C (DRAFT; cover and footers read 'CG25-1240-C Rev 0') |
| Issued | 2026-03-24 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | Blacksmith & Beard Sydney Airport Hotel Constructions (O'Riordan Street) Pty Ltd, PO Box 1222, Mascot NSW 1460 |
| Site | 237 O'Riordan Street, Mascot NSW (Bayside Council LGA); bounded by Ewan Street north, Sarah Street south, O'Riordan Street east, commercial premises west |
| Project | Proposed Mixed Use Building - multistorey hotel with three basement levels |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation (draft) for deep basement and foundation design |
| Extraction confidence | medium |

## Scope

Investigation for a mixed-use hotel with three basements next to an airport
tunnel asset. Three boreholes with SPTs, rock coring and standpipe installation,
laboratory testing, and advice on excavation, groundwater control, shoring
parameters, foundations, basement slabs, seismic subsoil class and aggressivity.

## Fieldwork

- BYDA search before drilling; specialist on-site services search
- Field investigation 25 to 27 February 2026 and 2 March 2026, logged to AS1726:2017
- Walkover survey of landform, surface conditions and adjacent structures
- Three boreholes BH01 to BH03 drilled with a track mounted rig to 30.32m, 12.5m and 30.5m respectively
- SPTs at regular intervals; NMLC rock coring after auger refusal at 21.4m (BH01) and 21.3m (BH03); core photographed
- Standpipes installed in all three boreholes to 12m depth, slotted screen 6m to 12m, sand/gravel filter to 5m, 1m bentonite seal 4m to 5m, site-derived backfill 0.5m to 4m, concrete seal in top 0.5m; wells developed with a submersible pump
- Groundwater observed during and shortly after drilling; long-term monitoring ongoing under a hydrogeologist
- Disturbed soil samples dispatched to NATA accredited laboratories under Chain of Custody

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Concrete slab; base 0.12m
- Unit 1 'Possibly' Fill: Silty SAND, fine grained, pale grey, low plasticity fines, moist, medium dense; base 0.3 - 0.4m
- Unit 2/3a Alluvium: SAND, fine grained, pale grey becoming pale orange, brown, trace low plasticity fines, moist to wet, loose to medium dense; base 6.2m
- Unit 3b Alluvium: SAND, fine grained, dark grey becoming grey, trace low plasticity fines, wet, medium dense to dense; base 10 - 16.2m
- Unit 3c Alluvium: Silty CLAY, high plasticity, dark grey, trace fine grained sand, moisture > plastic limit, very soft (BH01 and BH02 only); base >12.5 - 18.0m
- Unit 4 Residual: Silty CLAY, high plasticity, trace fine grained sand, grey, moisture > plastic limit, stiff to hard; base 20.5 - 21.4m
- Unit 5a Bedrock: SHALE, extremely weathered, fine grained, grey, very low strength with high plasticity clay bands, Class V (BH01 and BH03 only); base 24.0m
- Unit 5b Bedrock: SHALE, highly weathered, fine to medium grained, grey, low strength, Class IV (BH01 and BH03 only); base 26.7 - >30.32m
- Unit 5c Bedrock: SHALE, highly to moderately weathered, fine to medium grained, grey, low to medium strength, Class III (BH03 only); base >30.5m

## Rock

Shale of the Wianamatta sequence cored in BH01 and BH03 below about 21.3m to
21.4m, grading from extremely weathered Class V through highly weathered Class
IV to highly/moderately weathered Class III. Is50 values 0.075 to 1.7MPa (very
low to high strength), estimated UCS 1.125 to 25.5MPa. One laboratory UCS test
on BH01 core from 24.50-24.70m returned 4.3MPa.

## Groundwater

Encountered at about 3.0m to 3.2m below existing ground level during the field
investigation. Circulating water during diamond drilling in BH01 and BH03
prevented reliable measurement in those holes. Standpipes installed and longer-
term monitoring is in progress under a hydrogeologist. Permanent groundwater
lowering is generally not permitted, so the basement should be tanked; inflow
into a 12m deep excavation should be expected and temporary dewatering will
likely be required.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Borehole termination depths BH01 / BH02 / BH03 | 30.32 / 12.5 / 30.5 | m |
| Auger refusal depth, BH01 / BH03 | 21.4 / 21.3 | m |
| Groundwater depth at time of drilling | 3.0 to 3.2 | m below existing ground level |
| Anticipated maximum basement excavation depth | about 12 | m below existing ground surface |
| Field Moisture Content range (10 samples) | 20.1 to 34.4 | % |
| Is50 range | 0.075 to 1.7 | MPa |
| Estimated UCS range from Is50 | 1.125 to 25.5 | MPa |
| Laboratory UCS, BH01 24.50-24.70m | 4.3 | MPa |
| Aggressivity BH01 19.5-19.8m Silty Clay/Residual | FMC 17.0%, pH 6.8, conductivity 23 uS/cm, resistivity 440 Ohm.m, chloride <10 ppm, sulphate 36 ppm | - |
| Aggressivity BH03 18.0-18.45m Silty Sandy Clay/Alluvium | FMC 13.0%, pH 6.9, conductivity 16 uS/cm, resistivity 610 Ohm.m, chloride <10 ppm, sulphate 23 ppm | - |
| Seismic subsoil class (AS1170.4-2024) | De | - |
| Shoring parameters, 'Possibly' Fill Silty Sand Unit 2 | 17 kN/m3, c' 0 kPa, phi' 26 deg | - |
| Shoring parameters, Alluvium loose to medium Sand Unit 3a | 18 kN/m3, c' 0 kPa, phi' 28 deg | - |
| Shoring parameters, Alluvium medium dense to dense Sand Unit 3b | 20 kN/m3, c' 0 kPa, phi' 30 deg | - |
| Shoring parameters, Alluvium very soft Silty Clay Unit 3c | 14 kN/m3, c' 0 kPa, phi' 10 deg | - |
| Shoring parameters, Residual stiff to hard Silty Clay Unit 4 | 19 kN/m3, c' 5 kPa, phi' 20 deg | - |
| Shoring parameters, EW Shale Unit 5a | 22 kN/m3, c' 10 kPa, phi' 32 deg | - |
| Shoring parameters, HW Shale Unit 5b | 22 kN/m3, c' 50 kPa, phi' 33 deg | - |
| Shoring parameters, HW/MW Shale Unit 5c | 24 kN/m3, c' 100 kPa, phi' 34 deg | - |
| Foundation parameters, Shale Class V | 700 kPa serviceability end bearing, 100 kPa ultimate socket side shear, 50 MPa design Young's modulus | - |
| Foundation parameters, Shale Class IV | 1000 kPa serviceability end bearing, 150 kPa ultimate socket side shear, 150 MPa design Young's modulus | - |
| Foundation parameters, Shale Class III | 2000 kPa serviceability end bearing, 350 kPa ultimate socket side shear, 350 MPa design Young's modulus | - |
| Max PPV, historical or sensitive structures | 2 | mm/sec |
| Max PPV, residential and low rise buildings | 5 | mm/sec |
| Max PPV, brick or unreinforced structures in good condition | 10 | mm/sec |
| Max PPV, commercial/industrial reinforced concrete or steel | 25 | mm/sec |
| Excavation zone of influence | at least about 2 times the excavation depth behind the retained wall | - |
| Basement working platform | about 200mm loose thickness of DGB20 or similar fine crushed rock | - |
| Aggressivity classification (AS2159-2009) | non aggressive for concrete piles (Table 6.4.2(C)) and non aggressive for steel piles (Table 6.5.2(C)) | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Undertake dilapidation surveys of underground services and nearby structures before construction
- Prepare a vibration monitoring plan with trigger levels for demolition, excavation and piling, using the tabulated PPV limits confirmed by the structural engineer
- Design the basement as a tanked structure; permanent groundwater lowering is generally not permitted
- Provide an effective perimeter groundwater cut-off - diaphragm walls, secant piled walls, cutter soil mix walls or equivalent embedded walls; steel sheet piles are not preferred and soldier piles with shotcrete/lagging will not cut off groundwater in these sands
- Do not use ground anchors because of adjacent infrastructure, services, road reserves and the nearby airport tunnel; support progressively with internal bracing, strutting, raking props or top-down construction
- Embed the retained wall below final excavation level for toe stability and cut-off, allowing for over-excavation and local deeper pits
- Implement groundwater and deformation monitoring with trigger levels and contingency measures
- Do not assume a conventional raft is suitable; very soft high plasticity silty clay below the excavation level makes piled foundations or a piled raft more likely appropriate, with CFA piles founded in verified shale
- Control CFA pile installation to avoid soil decompression and ground disturbance; apply AS2159 strength reduction factors and undertake settlement analyses
- Place a 200mm DGB20 working platform on the inspected subgrade before basement slab and waterproofing works; ensure tanking continuity at joints, columns, piles and penetrations
- Adopt Subsoil Class De for seismic design per AS1170.4-2024
- Have the shoring and piling designs reviewed against this report, and have a geotechnical engineer inspect founding levels before concrete placement

## Stated limitations

- Draft document - status table records revision as DRAFT dated 24.03.2026 while cover and footers read Rev 0
- Prepared for the exclusive use of Blacksmith & Beard Sydney Airport Hotel Constructions (O'Riordan Street) Pty Ltd
- Conclusions based on available data and interpolation between boreholes; conditions may vary and may not become evident until construction
- Table 8 shoring parameters are indicative concept-level values from borehole logs, SPTs and engineering judgement, not laboratory derived
- UCS result is indicative of the sampled material only and may not represent the rock mass
- Site is an urban infill site where anthropogenic fill, buried structures and redundant services may be present
- Not to be used as part of a project specification without prior written CG agreement; must be read in its entirety with the Information Sheets

## Reviewer flags

DRAFT document - not issued. Table 4 (aggressivity) is column-scrambled in the
extraction; values mapped by header order. Several internal inconsistencies
worth resolving before issue: Section 1 describes thirteen storeys above ground
while Section 3 describes a ground level podium plus approximately eleven levels
above ground; Section 9.1 and Table 2 place the very soft high plasticity silty
clay in BH01 and BH02 (Section 9.1 says it was encountered in BH02 from about
12.0m), but Section 9.8 attributes it to BH01; Section 7.1 maps the site to the
Tuggerah Aeolian soil landscape, which sits oddly with the Mascot location and
the Sheet 9130 Quaternary Holocene (Qhd) geology cited in Section 7.2; Table 4's
caption reads 'Summary of Field Moisture Content Aggressivity Test Results';
Table 3 (FMC) has no caption row in the extraction; Section 8.3 contains a
truncated sentence ('The Is50 values for the ranged from...'). Table 5 in the
source lists 10 PLSI results, consistent with the Table 1 quantity.

## Standards cited

AS1726-2017 Geotechnical Site Investigations, AS2870-2011 Residential slabs and footings, AS2159-2009 Piling - Design and installation, AS3798-2007 Guidelines on earthworks for commercial and residential developments, AS1170.4-2024 Earthquake Actions in Australia, AS4133.4.1 (PLSI), AS4133.4.2.2 (UCS), AS1289 2.1.1 (FMC), APHA (soil aggressivity), Pells, Mostyn, Bertuzzi and Wong, Classification of Sandstones and Shales in the Sydney Region: A forty year review, Vol 54 No 2, June 2019, NSW Environment & Heritage eSPADE, Sydney 1:100,000 Geological Series Sheet 9130 (Edition 1) 1983

notes.title: CG25-1254-B - Queenscliff culvert replacement
notes.body:
# CG25-1254-B - Queenscliff culvert replacement

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG25-1254-B Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG25-1254-B Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2025-10-24 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd, Suite 2.01, 828 Pacific Highway, Gordon NSW 2072 |
| Site | Northern end of Queenscliff Beach NSW, on the sandstone rock platform adjacent to the ocean pool and promenade (Northern Beaches Council LGA) |
| Project | Proposed Culvert Replacement |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation for marine/intertidal remedial works |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Investigation of the ground beneath a dislodged stormwater culvert outlet in the
intertidal zone. Two cored boreholes and laboratory testing supported advice on
depth to bedrock, allowable bearing pressure, anchor design parameters, site
preparation and aggressivity for reinstatement of the outlet.

## Fieldwork

- BYDA search before drilling; specialist on-site services search
- Field investigation on 7 October 2025, logged to AS1726 (2017)
- Walkover survey of landform, site conditions and adjacent structures
- Two boreholes BH01 and BH02 cored by NMLC technique with portable rock coring equipment, terminated at 5.67m to 5.86m; 50mm hole size; core photographed
- Drilling contractor Tightsight Sampling Pty Ltd; BH01 R.L. surface 1.55m, BH02 R.L. surface 1.59m
- Selected rock core samples sent to NATA accredited laboratories under Chain of Custody
- Test locations measured from the supplied plan to about +/-1m

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Bedrock only: SANDSTONE, slightly weathered, fine grained, pale grey, yellow brown, few planar discontinuities, medium to wide spacing, oxide staining on some faces, surfaces mostly fresh to slightly stained, medium to high strength, Class III/II; base >5.67 - >5.86m

## Rock

Hawkesbury Sandstone (Rh), slightly weathered Class III/II, medium to high
strength, encountered from the rock platform surface to the base of both holes.
Is50 values 0.085 to 0.84MPa (very low to medium strength classification),
estimated UCS 1.27 to 12.6MPa. Eight PLSI tests: BH01 2.7-2.8m 0.56/0.31 Medium;
BH01 2.9-3.0m 0.72/0.44 Medium; BH01 3.9-4.0m 0.32/0.46 Medium; BH01 4.9-5.0m
0.37/0.74 Medium; BH02 2.94-3.0m 0.38/0.47 Medium; BH02 3.46-3.56m 0.085/0.27
Very Low; BH02 4.0-4.08m 0.37/0.24 Medium; BH02 5.58-5.6m 0.45/0.84 Medium
(diametral/axial MPa).

## Groundwater

No regional water table was measured. Drilling was within the intertidal zone
with the collar on the rock platform and the hole advancing in seawater from the
start, so observed water levels reflected tides and wave setup rather than
groundwater. Levels are expected to fluctuate rapidly with tides, swell and
rainfall, and seepage from the sandstone face may vary seasonally. No long-term
monitoring was undertaken.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Borehole termination depths | 5.67 to 5.86 | m |
| Hole size | 50 | mm |
| R.L. surface, BH01 / BH02 | 1.55 / 1.59 | m |
| Is50 range | 0.085 to 0.84 | MPa |
| Estimated UCS range | 1.27 to 12.6 | MPa |
| Allowable bearing pressure, Class III/II sandstone | 8 | MPa |
| Settlement criterion governing the ABP | total settlement not to exceed 1% of the minimum footing dimension | - |
| Ultimate compressive socket side shear for anchors/grouted dowels in Class III/II sandstone | 1,200 | kPa |
| Aggressivity, BH01 5.0-5.4m Sandstone/Bedrock | FMC 6.7%, pH 9.5, conductivity 828 uS/cm, resistivity 1,210 Ohm.cm, chloride 1,060 ppm, sulphate 250 ppm | - |
| Aggressivity, BH02 3.56-3.58m Sandstone/Bedrock | FMC 14.8%, pH 9.5, conductivity 686 uS/cm, resistivity 1,460 Ohm.cm, chloride 970 ppm, sulphate 240 ppm | - |
| Aggressivity classification (AS2159-2009) | Mild for concrete piles (Table 6.4.2(C)); Moderate for steel piles (Table 6.5.2(C)) | - |
| Laboratory testing quantities | 8 PLSI (AS4133.4.1); 1 aggressivity suite (APHA) | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Undertake dilapidation surveys of nearby structures before construction and have owners confirm the records
- Schedule work around low tide with standby allowance for adverse swell; install barriers, exclusion zones and spotters and keep emergency egress along the promenade and pool
- Secure permits for working on/near water, council land, maritime/coastal areas, heritage and ecology; locate subsurface services before demolition
- Treat any dewatering as temporary tide management only, not groundwater drawdown; discharge in accordance with regulations
- Plan lifts for restricted access using small plant or portable tools and secure equipment against wave action
- Design footings on Class III/II sandstone for an allowable bearing pressure of 8MPa, selecting a working pressure that keeps total settlement under 1% of the minimum footing dimension; reduce parameters where unfavourable defects, clay seams or open joints occur
- Design anchors and grouted dowels in Class III/II sandstone on an ultimate compressive socket side shear of 1,200 kPa, with cleaned sockets at R2 roughness or better and full grout contact
- Provide marine-grade corrosion protection for permanent anchors and locate bond zones below potential scour and beneath any weak weathered surface zone
- Proof-load representative anchors and record load-displacement before lock-off
- Clear founding areas of marine growth, debris and softened material and have them inspected before grout or concrete placement
- Govern durability design by the marine splash/tidal environment rather than the soil aggressivity results, which are typically less severe
- Keep records of hole cleanliness/roughness, grout pressures and volumes, proof-test results, as-built founding levels and photographs of prepared bearing surfaces

## Stated limitations

- Prepared for the exclusive use of H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd for the described development
- Conclusions based on interpolation between two boreholes; conditions can vary between test locations
- Depths and layer thicknesses in Table 2 apply to the investigation locations and may not represent the whole site
- Aggressivity ratings relate to soil contact conditions only
- Not to be used as part of a project specification without CG review and agreement; must be read in its entirety with the Information Sheets
- Listed further geotechnical inputs are hold points only; the contractor remains responsible for means, methods, temporary works and approvals

## Reviewer flags

Table 3 (aggressivity) is column-scrambled in the extraction; values mapped by
header order. Two minor text inconsistencies: Section 8.1 says 'Two (2) samples
were collected' while Table 1 records the aggressivity suite quantity as 1 (two
rows of results are reported); Section 7.2 describes the site as underlain by
'Wianamatta Group Hawkesbury Sandstone (Rh)' whereas Hawkesbury Sandstone sits
below the Wianamatta Group. Only bedrock was logged - no soil profile. Author
Jeevan Reddy, reviewer Raj Singh, approved 24.10.2025.

## Standards cited

AS1726-2017 Geotechnical Site Investigation, AS2159-2009 Piling - Design and Construction (Tables 6.4.2(C) and 6.5.2(C)), AS4133.4.1 (Point Load Strength Index), APHA (aggressivity suite), Pells, Mostyn, Bertuzzi and Wong, Classification of Sandstones and Shales in the Sydney Region: A forty year review, Vol 54 No 2, June 2019, Sydney 1:100,000 Geological Series Sheet 9130 (Edition 1) 1983

## Related notes

- [[AS 2159 piling]]
- [[Rock socket length]]
- [[Bored pier inspection]]
- [[Rock weathering classes]]
- [[Rock strength classes]]
- [[Weathered siltstone]]

notes.title: CG25-1430-A - Caddies Creek Reserve, Beaumont Hills
notes.body:
# CG25-1430-A - Caddies Creek Reserve, Beaumont Hills

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG25-1430-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG25-1430-A Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2026-01-18 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | Environmental Group Australia Pty Ltd, 36E Fitzroy Street, Marrickville NSW 2204 |
| Site | Caddies Creek Reserve Stage 2, Sanctuary Drive, Beaumont Hills NSW (The Hills Shire Council LGA) |
| Project | Proposed Caddies Creek Reserve Stage 2 - Football Centre of Excellence and associated reserve infrastructure |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Core Geotech investigated the Stage 2 reserve footprint to characterise ground
conditions for four soccer pitches, car parks and access roads, a Centre of
Excellence building, sports field lighting poles, and vehicle and pedestrian
bridges over Caddies Creek and an unnamed tributary. Work covered a walkover, 41
boreholes with in-situ testing, laboratory testing, and engineering advice on
earthworks, pavement design, foundations, groundwater and soil aggressivity.
Advice is preliminary and intended to support concept and early design
development.

## Fieldwork

- Site walkover survey and BYDA search plus contractor on-site services search
- 41 boreholes (BH01 to BH41) drilled with ute and track mounted rigs using 110 mm solid flight auger, terminated/refused at 2 m to 6.45 m
- 5 of those holes (BH32, BH33, BH39, BH40, BH41) extended by NMLC rock coring after auger refusal, to 8.12 m to 8.36 m
- DCP, pocket penetrometer and SPT testing in selected boreholes
- Groundwater observations during and shortly after drilling; holes backfilled by hand with spoil
- Disturbed sampling for NATA-accredited geotechnical and chemical laboratory testing
- Fieldwork undertaken on 28 October 2025, 2 to 6 November 2025, 13 November 2025, and 3, 10 and 11 December 2025

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Playing fields and turf areas (BH11-BH18, BH20-BH22, BH24-BH31, BH34) - Topsoil: silty clay/silty sand, fine to medium grained, grey, low plasticity fines, grass rootlets, moist; base 0.2-0.5 m
- Playing fields - Fill (local only): silty clay / silty sandy clay / clayey gravel / gravelly clay, low to high plasticity, brown and grey, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.5-2.5 m
- Playing fields - Alluvium: clay/silty clay, high plasticity, yellow, grey, brown grading to pale grey, moisture > plastic limit, stiff to very stiff; base >3.0-5.6 m
- Playing fields - Residual: clay, high plasticity, pale grey, red, orange, trace ironstone, moisture > plastic limit, stiff to very stiff; base 2.2->6.15 m
- Playing fields - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, fine to medium grained, grey/brown, very low strength, Class V, locally interbedded siltstone/laminite; base >4.5->6.45 m
- Carparks 1-3 and access road (BH01-BH10, BH35-BH38) - Topsoil: silty clay, medium plasticity, grey to brown, trace grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.2-0.3 m
- Carparks/access road - Fill: silty clay/silty sand/silty gravelly clay, low to medium plasticity with trace sand to gravel, moist to >= plastic limit; base 0.3-2.5 m
- Carparks/access road - Alluvium: silty clay/clay, medium to high plasticity, pale orange/red through grey to dark grey, trace fine sand or gravel locally, moisture commonly >= plastic limit; base >2.0->3.0 m
- Carparks/access road - Residual: silty clay, medium to high plasticity, red to pale orange to grey, trace fine sand and gravel, moisture >= plastic limit, generally very stiff; base 0.8-1.5 m
- Carparks/access road - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, fine grained, dark grey, very low to low strength, Class V; base >1.1->2.0 m
- Centre of Excellence building (BH19, BH23) - Fill: silty clay, medium plasticity, dark brown, trace sand and grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.5 m
- Centre of Excellence building - Residual: silty clay, medium plasticity, brown to grey brown, moisture < plastic limit, very stiff; base 1.6-1.7 m
- Centre of Excellence building - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, fine grained, grey becoming pale brown red, very low to low strength, Class V; base >4.5->5.0 m
- Bridges (BH32, BH33, BH39, BH40, BH41) - Topsoil: silty sandy clay, low plasticity, brown, fine to medium grained sand, grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.2 m
- Bridges - Fill (BH39 and BH41 only): silty sandy clay/silty clay, low to medium plasticity, brown, fine to medium sand, moisture < plastic limit; base 1.5-2.0 m
- Bridges - Alluvium: silty clay/clay, low to high plasticity, yellow and brown, moisture < plastic limit, stiff; base 2.7-3.2 m
- Bridges - Residual: silty clay/clay, low to high plasticity, brown, red, orange, pale grey with fine sand, moisture < plastic limit, stiff to very stiff; base 2.3-4.5 m
- Bridges - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, dark grey, very low to low strength, Class V, base 4.5-6.0 m; shale, highly weathered, grey, low strength, Class IV, base 5.3-6.85 m; siltstone/laminite, slightly weathered, dark grey, medium strength, Class III/IV, base 6.0->8.36 m; siltstone/laminite, slightly weathered, pale grey, medium to high strength, Class III, base >8.12->8.21 m
- Sports field lighting (BH11, BH14, BH15, BH16, BH22, BH26, BH27, BH29, BH30, BH34) - Topsoil base 0.2-0.5 m; Fill (silty clay/silty gravelly clay, low to medium plasticity) base 0.8-2.5 m; Alluvium (silty clay/clay, medium to high plasticity, mottled, very soft to very stiff) base 3.0-5.6 m; Residual clay (medium to high plasticity, locally trace shale fragments, stiff to very stiff) base 0.5->6.15 m; Bedrock extremely weathered shale Class V base >4.5->6.3 m

## Rock

Ashfield Shale (Wianamatta Group) was reached in most boreholes at variable
depth reflecting the floodplain setting. It is shallowest under the Centre of
Excellence building, where extremely weathered shale was met at about 1.6-1.7 m
in BH19 and BH23, and shallow in BH15 under the lighting area. Under the
pavements, extremely weathered Class V shale was logged from as shallow as about
1.1-2.0 m. At the bridge locations the cored profile runs from extremely
weathered Class V shale (base 4.5-6.0 m) through highly weathered Class IV shale
(base 5.3-6.85 m) into slightly weathered Class III/IV and Class III
siltstone/laminite of medium to high strength below about 6.0-8.2 m. Point load
Is(50) results on core ranged from 0.044 to 0.83 MPa diametral and 0.082 to 1.6
MPa axial, classified very low to high strength. No RLs are recorded on the
logs, so rockhead is expressed in depth only.

## Groundwater

Section 8.4 states groundwater was not encountered in BH12, BH18, BH20 to BH22,
BH24 to BH26, BH30, BH31, BH33, BH35 and BH36 to depths of 1.8 m to 5 m at the
time of investigation, and notes levels may not have stabilised over the short
observation window. Circulating water used for the cored holes (BH32, BH33,
BH39, BH40, BH41) prevented any water level measurement. Later sections report
groundwater as encountered: about 1.8 m in BH35 and about 2 m in BH36 (Carpark
3), about 5 m in BH30 and about 2 m in BH31 (Field 4), and about 3 m in BH22, 5
m in BH26 and 5 m in BH30 (lighting). No standpipes or longer-term monitoring

tell you.

## Recommendations

- Strip topsoil across turf footprints and stockpile separately for reuse where the environmental consultant approves
- Treat all fill as uncontrolled unless placement and compaction records are produced
- Remove fill and unsuitable, disturbed or compressible material to expose competent natural subgrade, then inspect and proof roll before any filling
- Undercut and replace soft or pumping zones with engineered fill or imported granular material; use a temporary working platform where wet conditions persist
- Place all filling as engineered fill under Level 2 geotechnical control to AS 3798-2007 for fields and pavements, and Level 1 control for the Centre of Excellence building pad
- Set geotechnical hold points at completion of stripping, after soft spot treatment, before fill placement, and at acceptance of final platform level
- Stage earthworks to limit trafficking of exposed clay subgrades and re-proof roll after rain
- Expect localised very soft alluvium in Fields 2 and 3 near BH12 and allow extra undercut and replacement there
- For Field 4, plan deep fill removal (up to about 2.5 m) allowing for wet excavation and groundwater inflow, particularly near BH31, with sump pumping and staged excavation
- Adopt a preliminary design subgrade CBR of 3% for Carparks 1-3 and the access road, and confirm with further CBR testing after trimming and proof rolling
- Provide a capping layer beneath pavements and maintain positive drainage during construction and in the final works
- Use DGB20 base to TfNSW QA Specification 3051, compacted in layers not exceeding 200 mm loose
- Provide perimeter subsoil drains with invert at least 200 mm below pavement formation, connected to the site stormwater system
- Reassess AS 2870 differential movement after earthworks and immediately before building pad construction; design slabs using engineering principles allowing for reactivity
- For the Centre of Excellence building, either pad/strip footings at 150 kPa embedded at least 0.8 m, or shallow bored piers socketed at least 0.6 m into competent extremely weathered shale
- Pour high level footings promptly after excavation and cleaning; use 75 mm blinding concrete if the pour is delayed and prevent ponding in footing bases

- Ignore shaft resistance in the upper 1.8 m of reactive clay for piled footings and use 50% of compression shaft adhesion as an uplift screening value
- Use deep foundations for the vehicle and pedestrian bridges, with rock-socketed bored piers taken 1 to 2 m into competent Class III rock and founded below the design scour level
- Allow for temporary casing or drilling fluids through soft alluvium and below groundwater, and consider downdrag where new fill is placed
- Inspect all footing excavations, pile bores and rock sockets before reinforcement and concreting to confirm founding material, socket depth, cleanliness and groundwater inflow
- Use tremie placement where groundwater inflow prevents a dry founding surface
- Have CG review civil, structural, architectural and landscape drawings and the contractor's earthworks methodology before construction
- Re-engage CG if conditions differ materially from those described or if the design, layout or site levels change

## Stated limitations

- Prepared exclusively for Environmental Group Australia Pty Ltd, for the described development and purpose only, under CG's Terms of Engagement and proposal QU25-0109 Rev 0 dated 10 January 2025
- Conclusions rely on interpolation between boreholes; conditions can vary between test locations in ways the investigation cannot define
- Depths and layer thicknesses in Tables 2 to 6 are indicative only and may not represent the whole site
- No detailed contour survey was available at the time of reporting; site levels are based on walkover observations and aerial imagery
- Test locations were measured from the supplied plan to an accuracy of about +/- 5 m
- Groundwater levels may not have stabilised over the short observation period; no longer-term monitoring was undertaken and levels can fluctuate with rainfall, temperature and other factors
- Circulating water in the cored holes prevented groundwater measurement
- Foundation and pavement parameters are preliminary, to be confirmed by the structural and pavement designers and by construction-stage inspection
- AS 2870 provisions do not strictly apply to the Centre of Excellence building because of its size; the classification given is preliminary
- The report should not be used as part of a project specification without CG review and agreement, and must be kept whole and read with the attached Information Sheets
- Information supplied by the client and their agents was relied on and not independently verified

schedules 20 PLSI tests. Minor typos in the source: 'laminate' is used for
'laminite' in Section 10.6, and Section 10.4.1 reads 'are likely produce'.
