notes.body:
# CG26-0172-A - Osroy Avenue stormwater, Earlwood

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG26-0172-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG26-0172-A Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2026-02-25 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd, Suite 2.01, 828 Pacific Highway, Gordon NSW 2072 |
| Site | Steep vegetated corridor between Bayview Lane and Homer Street, off Osroy Avenue, Earlwood NSW (City of Canterbury Bankstown LGA) |
| Project | Proposed stormwater upgrade from Osroy Avenue to Homer Street, for Canterbury Bankstown Council |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation with AGS 2007 qualitative landslide risk assessment |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Core Geotech characterised the ground along the nominated rockface corridor for
a stormwater drainage upgrade and assessed slope instability hazards and risk
qualitatively to AGS (2007). Two concept options were considered: an open
channel of about 400 mm by 500 mm internal dimensions, or a nominally DN600
pipeline partly fixed above ground to the rockface with brackets and rock
anchors, possibly with intermediate drop structures. The assessment supports
concept planning and approvals only and excludes detailed design of
stabilisation, anchors, structural supports or temporary works; the client
advised that other parts of the broader drainage upgrade did not need
investigation.

## Fieldwork

- Site walkover survey and BYDA search plus contractor on-site services search
- 2 boreholes (BH01 and BH02) drilled on 3 February 2026 by Tightsight Sampling Pty Ltd, hand auger in soil and NMLC coring in rock with portable rock coring equipment, hole size 125 mm
- BH01 terminated at 4.13 m (surface RL 29.49 m); BH02 terminated at 3.77 m (surface RL 30.55 m)
- DCP tests carried out adjacent to the boreholes (DCP = 0 at BH01 surface, DCP = 7 at BH02 surface, with double bounce recorded at refusal)
- Rock core photographed and groundwater observations recorded during and shortly after drilling; boreholes backfilled by hand with spoil
- Disturbed soil and rock sampling for NATA-accredited laboratory testing (8 PLSI tests, 1 aggressivity suite)

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Unit 1 - Fill: silty sandy CLAY, low plasticity, grey, fine to medium grained sand, some grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.3-1.1 m
- Unit 2 - 'Probable' Residual (BH01 only): sandy CLAY, medium plasticity, brown and pale grey, fine to medium grained sand, moisture < plastic limit; base 1.5 m
- Unit 3a - Bedrock (BH01 only): SANDSTONE, extremely weathered, fine to medium grained, red, brown, pale grey, very low strength; base 1.69 m
- Unit 3c - Bedrock: sandstone, highly weathered, fine to medium grained, brown, very low strength, highly fractured to disaggregated, locally friable with soil-like infill, interpreted as a weathered seam or defect zone; base 2.85 m
- Unit 3b - Bedrock: SANDSTONE, slightly weathered, fine to medium grained, red and pale grey becoming grey, low to medium strength, Class IV/III; base >3.77 m (BH02) to >4.13 m (BH01)

## Rock

Hawkesbury Sandstone was reached in both holes. Extremely weathered very low
strength sandstone was logged in BH01 from about 1.5 m to 1.69 m; in BH02 the
fill passes into cored rock from about 0.3 m. Section 10.3 states competent
Class IV/III sandstone occurs at relatively shallow depth, typically below about
0.3 m to 1.69 m below existing ground level at the borehole locations. A
distinctly weaker highly weathered horizon (Unit 3c) was encountered in BH02 at
approximately 2.43 m to 2.85 m and may be localised. Point load Is(50) values
for the Hawkesbury Sandstone ranged from 0.0064 to 0.77 MPa, corresponding to
very low to medium strength, with estimated UCS of 0.096 to 11.55 MPa.

## Groundwater

Not encountered at the time of investigation. Both borehole logs record
GROUNDWATER NOT ENCOUNTERED. Circulating water used for the diamond drilling
prevented any groundwater level measurement. The report notes standing
groundwater and seepage can fluctuate with rainfall, temperature and other
factors.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Serviceability end bearing pressure, Hawkesbury Sandstone Class IV/III | 3000 | kPa |
| Ultimate compressive socket side shear, Hawkesbury Sandstone Class IV/III | 500 | kPa |
| Design Young's modulus, Hawkesbury Sandstone Class IV/III | 350 | MPa |
| Settlement basis for the quoted end bearing pressure | less than 1% of minimum footing dimension | - |
| Settlement at which ultimate socket side shear is mobilised | greater than 5% of minimum footing dimension | - |
| Point load Is(50) range, Hawkesbury Sandstone | 0.0064 to 0.77 | MPa |
| Estimated UCS range, Hawkesbury Sandstone | 0.096 to 11.55 | MPa |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - field moisture content | 2.5 | % |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - pH | 6.2 | - |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - electrical conductivity | 25 | uS/cm |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - resistivity | 40000 | Ohm.cm |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - chloride | 10 | ppm |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - sulphate | 10 | ppm |
| Aggressivity classification for concrete piles (AS 2159 Table 6.4.2(C)) | Mild, high permeability soils type A | - |
| Aggressivity classification for steel piles (AS 2159 Table 6.5.2(C)) | non aggressive, high permeability soils type A | - |
| Overall existing slope instability risk (AGS 2007 qualitative) | low to medium | - |
| Risk rating - rockfall from loosened blocks | Possible likelihood, Major consequence, High risk | - |
| Risk rating - localised wedge or toppling instability | Unlikely to Possible, Major, Medium to High | - |
| Risk rating - ravelling and shallow sloughing of soil or weathered sandstone | Possible, Moderate, Medium | - |
| Risk rating - construction induced loosening during drilling and fixing | Possible, Moderate to Major, Medium to High | - |
| Risk rating - fixings founded in highly weathered or weak sandstone bands | Unlikely to Possible, Moderate to Major, Medium to High | - |
| Risk rating - degraded legacy support elements or surface treatments | Unlikely to Possible, Major, Medium | - |
| Risk rating - water ingress, erosion or local undercutting | Unlikely to Possible, Moderate, Low to Medium | - |
| Risk rating - access and working at height constraints | Possible, Major, High | - |
| Option 1 open channel nominal internal dimensions | approximately 400 by 500 | mm |
| Option 2 pipeline nominal diameter | DN600 | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Treat the fill as uncontrolled under AS 2870-2011 because no placement, material or compaction records exist
- Carry out dilapidation surveys of underground services and nearby structures before construction, and have owners confirm the records
- Avoid conventional shallow footings for the stormwater infrastructure and support structures because of steep terrain, rock outcrop and variable near-surface materials
- Found supports, thrust blocks, headwalls, pits and pier supports in competent Class IV/III sandstone at depth
- Design socketed elements to extend past any highly weathered or low strength sandstone zone, such as the Unit 3c horizon logged in BH02
- Verify founding conditions at every rock anchor and bracket location; anchors must sit in competent sandstone, not in highly weathered bands, with proof testing where required
- Confirm final founding level and socket length during construction by inspecting excavations, reviewing drilling spoil and drill response, and short confirmatory coring where needed
- Establish delineated exclusion zones along the Homer Street footpath where required
- Have a suitably experienced geotechnical consultant carry out staged inspection of the rockface at and above proposed fixing locations, with scaling or removal of loose material where identified
- Do not assume the presence, condition or support function of legacy rock bolts and shotcrete without inspection
- Control stormwater discharge and temporary diversions and protect against scour at drop structures and outlets
- Undertake targeted supplementary investigation (test pits or short cores) at critical support locations where weaker weathered sandstone bands are suspected
- Review final civil and structural drawings and the contractor's methodology, including access arrangements and footpath protection
- Implement geotechnical inspection hold points at each support location before drilling and during socketing, and adjust socket lengths as needed
- Complete a post-installation inspection with periodic follow-up checks after major rainfall events
- Select concrete and steel appropriate to the assessed aggressivity
- Re-review the assessment once the final alignment, fixing locations and construction methodology are confirmed, or if the works materially change drainage, slope geometry or crest/toe loading

## Stated limitations

- Prepared exclusively for H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd for the described development and purpose, under CG's Terms of Engagement and proposal QU25-0483 Rev 0 dated 28 October 2025
- The slope stability assessment is qualitative, indicative and based on a walkover plus limited boreholes and coring; it is not a detailed design of stabilisation measures, anchor systems, structural supports or temporary works
- Ratings reflect conditions at the time of inspection and may change once the final alignment and fixing locations are set, vegetation is cleared or drainage patterns are altered
- Depths and layer thicknesses in Table 2 are based on the two investigation locations and may not represent the whole site
- Test locations were measured from the supplied plan to an accuracy of about +/- 3 m
- Circulating water precluded groundwater measurement during diamond drilling; standing water and seepage can fluctuate seasonally
- Is(50) testing is not readily performed on extremely low to very low strength rock, so strength classification for weaker sequences relied on visual and tactile assessment
- Geotechnical design parameters are for preliminary sizing only; detailed foundation sizing and structural design remain with the project structural designer
- Vegetation, soil mantle and leaf litter obscure rock exposures and may conceal loosened blocks, open joints and debris
- Conclusions rely on interpolation between discrete test locations; variations between them cannot be explicitly defined
- Must not be used as part of a construction specification without CG's written agreement, and must be kept and reproduced whole with the attached Information Sheets

## Reviewer flags

Extraction is clean throughout; the narrative, Table 2 (strata), Table 4 (PLSI),
Table 5 (risk matrix) and Table 6 (foundation parameters) all read reliably. Two
caveats. Table 3 (aggressivity) has rotated column headers that extracted as a
vertical jumble; the single data row reads 2.5 / 6.2 / 25 / 40,000 / 10 / 10 and
I have mapped these to moisture content, pH, conductivity, resistivity, chloride
and sulphate in header order, which is consistent, but confirm against the
source PDF. Second, there is a small internal inconsistency in depth reporting
for the weak Unit 3c horizon: Table 2 gives its base at 2.85 m without an upper
bound or a borehole attribution, while Section 10.3 places it in BH02 at
approximately 2.43 m to 2.85 m; I have carried both. Note also that unlike the
companion report, RLs are present here (BH01 surface RL 29.49 m, BH02 surface RL
30.55 m, datum stated only as 'm'), so rockhead can be expressed as RL if
needed. No AS 2870 site classification is given because the works are drainage
infrastructure, not residential slabs and footings; AS 2870 is cited only for
the uncontrolled-fill definition. Also note Section 7.2 describes Hawkesbury
Sandstone as a 'Wianamatta Group' subgroup, which is a geological error in the
source (Hawkesbury Sandstone underlies the Wianamatta Group).

## Standards cited

AS 1726-2017, AS 2870-2011, AS 2159-2009, AS 3798-2007, AS 4133.4.1, HB 160-2006, AGS Landslide Risk Management Concepts and Guidelines (2007), Australian Geomechanics Vol 42 No 1 March 2007, Australian Geoguide LR8 (Construction Practice), APHA (aggressivity suite)

notes.title: CG26-0496-A - Toukley boat ramp
notes.body:
# CG26-0496-A - Toukley boat ramp

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG26-0496-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG26-0496-A Rev 0 (cover page reads 'Ref: CG26-0496 Rev 0') |
| Issued | 2026-04-17 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | EGA Pty Ltd, 36E Fitzroy Street, Marrickville NSW 2204 |
| Site | 20 Peel Street, Toukley NSW - foreshore of Tuggerah Lake, adjacent to Marine Rescue Tuggerah Lakes |
| Project | Proposed Boat Ramp Works (Toukley Marine Rescue boat ramp) |
| Document type | preliminary geotechnical investigation (land-based) |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Land-based borehole investigation to support concept design of a boat ramp,
accessways and foreshore works. Covers subsurface profile, groundwater,
laboratory testing, ramp support options, preliminary pile founding parameters,
scour protection and aggressivity. The submerged portion of the ramp was not
investigated and is addressed by extrapolation.

## Fieldwork

- BYDA search before drilling; specialist on-site services search
- Field investigation on 1 April 2026, logged generally to AS1726:2017
- Site walkover of landform, site conditions and adjacent structures
- One borehole BH01 drilled with a Comacchio GEO 305 track mounted rig, 120mm continuous flight augers to 4.7m, with SPTs
- NMLC rock coring from 4.7m to termination at 10.37m; core photographed
- Groundwater observed during drilling and shortly after completion
- Disturbed soil and rock samples submitted to a NATA accredited laboratory under Chain of Custody
- Borehole backfilled by hand with excavated spoil
- Borehole location set out from the supplied plan to about +/-3m

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Road Base: Compacted road base material at surface; base 0.2m
- Fill: Silty SAND, fine grained, grey, brown with low plasticity fines, moisture condition = wet; base 0.7m
- Alluvium: Silty SAND, fine grained, grey with low plasticity fines, wet, loose to medium dense; base 1.7m
- Alluvium: Silty CLAY, medium to high plasticity, red brown to pale brown, yellow grey with some sand, moisture <= plastic limit, firm to stiff; base 4.5m
- Bedrock: SHALE, highly weathered, fine to medium grained, yellowish brown, very low strength; base 4.7m
- Bedrock: Conglomeratic Sandstone, moderately to highly weathered, light grey to pale brown, very coarse grained, rounded to subrounded gravel sized clasts in a finer sandy matrix, low to medium strength; base >10.37m

## Rock

Highly weathered very low strength shale from 4.5m to 4.7m over moderately to
highly weathered conglomeratic sandstone to beyond 10.37m. Is50 0.14 to 0.56MPa,
indicating low to medium strength, with estimated UCS of about 2MPa to 9MPa.
Weaker, highly weathered samples could not be tested and were classified by
visual and tactile assessment.

## Groundwater

Encountered in BH01 at about 0.6m depth at the time of investigation.
Circulating water during diamond drilling prevented measurement of levels in the
cored section. Standing groundwater and seepage may fluctuate with rainfall and
temperature; the low-lying foreshore setting means shallow groundwater influence
and water level fluctuation in nearshore soils are considered likely.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Borehole termination depth, BH01 | 10.37 | m |
| Auger depth before coring | 4.7 | m |
| Borehole diameter | 120 | mm |
| Groundwater depth in BH01 | about 0.6 | m |
| Field Moisture Content, alluvial soils | 19.5 to 34.4 | % |
| Field Moisture Content, weathered bedrock (shale, 4.5-4.95m) | 20.3 | % |
| Aggressivity, BH01 5.1-5.2m Conglomeratic Sandstone/Bedrock | FMC 3.5%, pH 9.0, conductivity 42 uS/cm, resistivity 23,800 Ohm.cm, chloride <10 ppm, sulphate <10 ppm | - |
| Is50, BH01 5.54-5.68m | 0.14 diametral / 0.56 axial - Low strength | MPa |
| Is50, BH01 7.46-7.58m | 0.31 diametral / 0.37 axial - Medium strength | MPa |
| Is50, BH01 10.14-10.27m | 0.25 diametral / 0.39 axial - Medium strength | MPa |
| Estimated UCS range | about 2 to 9 | MPa |
| Allowable end bearing pressure, piles in moderately weathered rock | up to 1000 | kPa |
| Allowable end bearing pressure, piles in very stiff alluvial silty clay | 400 | kPa |
| Ultimate shaft adhesion, very stiff alluvial silty clay | 50 | kPa (for embedment below about 1.5m beneath the lake bed) |
| Rock mattress minimum thickness (landward portion) | about 600 | mm |
| Depth to firm alluvial clay for rock mattress founding | about 1.5 to 1.7 | m |
| Aggressivity classification (AS2159-2009) | mild for concrete piles (Table 6.4.2(C)); non aggressive for steel piles (Table 6.5.2(C)); stated as applying to high permeability soils (type B) | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Rock mattress option: excavate uncontrolled fill and loose sandy alluvium to expose firm alluvial clay (about 1.5-1.7m), place a 600mm minimum rock mattress of durable cobbles and boulders, install a geotextile or geogrid separator, then compacted DGB or DGS40 and the concrete ramp slab; use larger boulders in the submerged portion
- Piled support option: driven or bored piles founded in very stiff alluvial silty clay or rock, more applicable to a floating pontoon or suspended ramp; detailed pile design required
- Land-based slab option: slab on ground after removal of uncontrolled fill and loose alluvium and replacement with controlled engineered fill to AS3798 - not suitable for the submerged or nearshore portion
- Detail the design to accommodate localised differential settlement, particularly at the transition between land-based and submerged sections
- Provide rock scour protection over a geotextile filter at the ramp toe and along the submerged portion; confirm extent, thickness and rock grading during detailed design
- Treat the existing fill as uncontrolled in accordance with AS3798-2007 since no records were available
- Undertake a project specific geotechnical assessment once the concept design is finalised; have CG review civil and structural drawings
- Inspect the ramp subgrade after excavation and confirm founding conditions before basecourse and concrete; place controlled fill under Level 1 supervision to AS3798-2007

## Stated limitations

- Investigation was land-based only; the submerged portion of the ramp was not directly assessed and comments there rely on extrapolation
- Only one borehole was drilled; the subsurface profile is expected to vary laterally, particularly towards the lake
- Pile founding parameters are preliminary and must be confirmed during detailed design and construction
- Based on concept level information; any change to layout, levels or structural system requires review
- Prepared for the exclusive use of EGA Pty Ltd for the described development
- Must be read in its entirety with the attached Information Sheets; not to be used as a project specification without CG's written agreement

## Reviewer flags

Table 4 (aggressivity) is column-scrambled in the extraction; values mapped by
header order. Document identity is inconsistent: cover reads 'Ref: CG26-0496 Rev
0' and 17 April 2026, the document status table reads CG26-0496-A Rev 0 dated
08.04.2026, and footers read CG26-0496-A Rev 0 / 17 April 2026. Consistency
issue on clay consistency: Table 2 describes the alluvial silty clay as 'firm to
stiff', while Section 9.2 and the pile parameters in Section 9.4 refer to 'very
stiff' alluvial silty clay (the BH01 log records the SPT interval as Very
stiff). Prepared by Jeevan Reddy, reviewed by Raj Singh.

## Standards cited

AS1726-2017 Geotechnical Site Investigation, AS2870-2011 Residential slabs and footings, AS2159-2009 Piling - Design and installation, AS3798-2007 Guidelines on earthworks for commercial and residential developments, AS4133.4.1 (PLSI), AS1289 2.1.1 (FMC), APHA (aggressivity/pH), NSW Boat Ramp Facility Guidelines, Transport for NSW, September 2015, NSW Environment & Heritage eSPADE, Gosford-Lake Macquarie Special 1:100,000 Geological Sheet 9131 and part sheet 9231

## Related notes

- [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]]
- [[AS 2159 piling]]

notes.title: AS 1726 soil and rock description
notes.body:
# AS 1726 soil and rock description

AS 1726:2017 *Geotechnical site investigations* is the Australian standard that
sets out how ground is described and logged. It is the reason two engineers
logging the same core should produce comparable descriptions.

> The standard itself is copyright and is not reproduced here. Clause numbers
> are recorded so the passage can be found; check the actual document before
> relying on any of this on a job.

## What it governs

- The vocabulary for soil and rock description, and the order terms appear in —
  see [[Soil description order]].
- Weathering and strength classification for rock — see
  [[Rock weathering classes]] and [[Rock strength classes]].
- Sampling and in-situ test reporting requirements.
- What a borehole log must show — see [[Borehole log conventions]].

## Why the order matters

The description order is not stylistic. A log is read by people scanning a
column for a change in material, so the governing term comes first and the
qualifiers follow. Writing "brown clay, high plasticity" instead of
"CLAY: high plasticity, brown" breaks the scan.

## Related

- [[AS 2159 piling]] — founding requirements that rely on these descriptions
- [[Weathered siltstone]] — the description applied on most of our Sydney work

notes.title: AS 2159 piling
notes.body:
# AS 2159 piling

AS 2159:2009 *Piling — Design and installation* governs pile design and
construction, including bored piers.

> Summarised, not reproduced. Clause references are pointers, not quotations.

## What we lean on it for

- **Base cleanliness and concrete placement.** Clause 7.6.5(c) is the one cited
  in most of our inspection reports: loose or softened material at the base is
  removed before concrete, and concrete follows promptly after drilling,
  cleaning and geotechnical approval. See [[Bored pier inspection]].
- **Founding verification.** The pier is proved into the material the design
  assumed, not merely to a nominated depth.
- **Risk rating and the geotechnical strength reduction factor.** The standard
  ties the factor to how much site investigation and construction control there
  actually is — better investigation earns a higher factor.

## The practical consequence for inspections

Our sign-off is that the exposed founding material was competent and consistent
with the design assumption at the time of inspection. That is a narrower claim
than "the pile is adequate", and the report wording keeps it narrow. Acceptance
of the pile as a structural element remains with the design engineer — see
[[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]].

## Related

- [[Rock socket length]]
- [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]]

notes.title: AS 2870 residential site classification
notes.body:
# AS 2870 residential site classification

AS 2870 *Residential slabs and footings* classifies sites by how much the soil
moves with moisture change, which then drives the footing design.

> Summarised. Class definitions and design tables live in the standard.

## Classes in short

- **A** — stable, little or no ground movement from moisture change (sand, rock)
- **S** — slightly reactive clay
- **M** — moderately reactive clay or silt
- **H1 / H2** — highly reactive clay
- **E** — extremely reactive clay
- **P** — problem site: fill, soft soil, mine subsidence, landslip, or where the
  above cannot be applied

## What decides the class

Characteristic surface movement `y_s`, calculated from soil reactivity and the
depth of the design suction change. Reactivity comes from shrink-swell index
testing, not from the description alone — a clay that looks the same in two
suburbs can classify differently.

## The trap

Fill, cut, and trees change the answer. A site with uncontrolled fill is P
regardless of the clay underneath it, and removing a large tree can leave years
of ongoing heave. Classification without checking site history is guesswork.

## Related

- [[Soil description order]]
- [[DCP testing]]
